subject: Intermittent token pacing spike on LiveChat — playbook + post-incident notes
messages:
From: Ava Turner <ava.turner@siena.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Siena Ops <ops@siena.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Erratic token pacing in LiveChat during 14:05–14:30 PDT

Hi Chloe / Laura,

Wanted to flag an issue we saw during our afternoon peak (approx 14:05–14:30 PDT) where LiveChat sessions started stalling mid-response — tokens would emit for 2–3s and then pause for 6–12s before continuing. This affected about ~8% of sessions for users hitting our realtime route (model=redwood-large-stream, streaming=true).

Impact: several agents reported partial responses and customers saw long "typing" pauses. We captured a short recording and a trace (attached minimal replayer) showing the pause corresponds to repeated 504s on the client socket while the server ultimately resumed.

We've temporarily throttled concurrency on our side and routed a subset of traffic to non-streaming fallback, but this hurts our SLA with agents. Can Redwood share immediate mitigation suggestions (client-side knobs we can apply) and any ETA on investigation?

Attached: small trace extract (repro-trace-20280629.json)

Thanks,
Ava Turner
Platform & Integrations
Siena Labs
[attachment: repro-trace-20280629.json]
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Ava Turner <ava.turner@siena.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Siena Ops <ops@siena.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Erratic token pacing in LiveChat during 14:05–14:30 PDT

Hi Ava — thanks for the quick heads up and for the repro trace. We’re opening an SR internally and Ben (infra) is already looking at server-side traces.

Immediate short-term customer-side mitigations we recommend while we triage:
- Enable streaming fallback: set streaming=false for critical agent sessions — this trades latency for reliability while we stabilize.
- Reduce max_tokens_per_chunk to 32 (if you’re using chunking) — this reduces long-tail KV cache window pressure.
- Set client reconnect backoff to 250–500ms instead of aggressive reconnects to avoid amplifying edge congestion.

I attached a brief playbook with these steps and a simple curl snippet to toggle streaming. Ben will follow up with what he's seeing server-side and a proposed timeline.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep this prioritized.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Erratic token pacing in LiveChat during 14:05–14:30 PDT — initial triage

Hi all — quick triage notes from infra:

What we observed
- Between 14:03–14:28 PDT we saw a spike in requests that aligned with Siena’s traffic pattern. Several inference workers hit bursts of long-tail token emission where kernel execution paused for multiple seconds.
- Root cause (interim): a cascade where large prefix KV cache evictions + a quantized attention code-path mismatch caused temporary thread stalls on a subset of GPU nodes. That led to increased per-request tail latency, which in turn created backpressure on the connection layer.

Temporary mitigations we applied (15:10–15:40)
- Pinned Siena traffic to a different host pool (rebalanced) to isolate from affected nodes.
- Flushed and warmed the KV cache proactively for your model shards.
- Deployed a conservative scheduler override: lower simultaneous decoding threads per GPU for the affected nodes (reduces throughput but reduces tail probability).

Customer-facing recommendations (short-term)
- As Chloe suggested, toggle streaming=false for high-SLA agent workflows while we complete the fix.
- Set max_tokens_per_chunk=32 and prefer smaller prompt prefixes where feasible.
- If you can tolerate small added latency, enable response-aggregation at your client to hide micro-pauses (batch small token chunks client-side before rendering).

Next steps & ETA
- Engineering is reproducing the eviction -> kernel-path interaction locally (we have a repro trace; see attached). We expect a targeted runtime patch within 48 hours to remove the stall path and a follow-up rollout across Dedicated pools within 5 business days.

I’ll send a brief post-incident summary with the timeline and permanent mitigations once the patch ships. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize Siena’s traffic until the fix is in.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident: LiveChat pacing spike resolved + recommended next steps

Hi Ava / Siena Ops team — final summary from Redwood. Thank you for working through this with us.

What happened (summary)
- Window: 2028-06-29 14:03–14:28 PDT.
- Symptom: intermittent multi-second pauses in token delivery on streaming endpoints for ~8% of Siena sessions.
- Root cause: interaction between large prefix KV cache evictions and a quantized attention kernel selection edge-case on a subset of inference workers which caused thread stalls.

What we did- Isolated affected hosts and rebalanced traffic within 40 minutes.
- Flushed/warmed KV caches for your shard and reduced concurrent decoding threads on the affected pool.
- Deployed a temporary scheduler override to prevent the stall path while the fix was built.

Customer action & recommended configuration (to avoid exposure until full patch)- For critical agent-facing sessions: streaming=false (recommended for SLA-sensitive flows).
- If you need streaming, set max_tokens_per_chunk=32 and avoid very large prompt prefixes (>=8k tokens).
- Apply client-side reconnect backoff (250–500ms) and enable small response-aggregation.

Permanent fix & timeline- We have a runtime patch that removes the kernel-path stall and improves eviction sequencing; it has passed internal tests and will roll out to Dedicated pools on Tue, Jul 2 (target).
- We’ll monitor Siena’s shard for 72 hours after rollout and provide a short verification report.

Credits & next steps- As a gesture for the impact, we’re applying a one-time service credit to your July invoice; finance will follow up.
- Ben and I will schedule a 30-minute sync next week to walk through the technical details and answer any questions. Please let me know a few windows that work.

Apologies again for the disruption. Attached is the short mitigation playbook with client snippets and the repro trace we used.

Best regards,
